checks.title: Requested variables present in source files
checks.message: All 33 raw variables found in 10 file(s).

checks.title: Real vs synthetic data
checks.message: Official source files were used (MD5 recorded in provenance).

checks.title: Appropriate sample weight
checks.message: mec weight (WTMECPRP) matches the most restrictive component used; weights rescaled by cycle length when combining cycles.

checks.title: Analytic weights positive and non-missing
checks.message: 0 analytic records with missing/zero weight. Weighted population represented: 228.9 million.

checks.title: Design degrees of freedom
checks.message: Analytic population spans 49 PSUs in 24 strata (df = 25). NCHS flags estimates with df < 8.

checks.title: Events per model parameter
checks.message: 1274 events, 5427 non-events, 16 parameters -> 79.6 per parameter (rule of thumb >= 10).

checks.title: Outcome missingness
checks.message: 1.0% of the eligible population lacks the outcome (91 of 8878). Missing outcome is assumed missing at random within the design.

checks.title: Complete-case loss
checks.message: 18.2% of the analytic sample (1486) lack >=1 covariate. Multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis recommended.

checks.title: Raw values within plausible ranges
checks.message: Out-of-range values: BMXBMI (0 low, 1 high); BPXODI1 (0 low, 1 high); BPXOSY1 (1 low, 0 high); BPXOSY2 (2 low, 0 high); BPXOSY3 (2 low, 0 high); LBXGH (1 low, 0 high); URDACT (0 low, 2 high)

checks.title: NCHS presentation standards for proportions
checks.message: 11 of 11 estimates meet the standard; 0 should be suppressed, 0 flagged for review.

checks.title: No implausible effect sizes
checks.message: All ratio estimates within 0.1-10 with SE(log) < 2.5.

checks.title: Model size vs design degrees of freedom
checks.message: Primary model has 17 parameters; design df = 25. Wald tests and CIs use the design df (t distribution).

checks.title: Sensitivity analyses agree with primary result
checks.message: 5 of 5 sensitivity analyses agree in direction (associations) or magnitude (prevalence).

checks.title: Age top-coding
checks.message: NHANES top-codes age at 80 years; age is modelled as continuous with this censoring.

checks.title: Derived variables computable
checks.message: 30 derived variables computed; see derivation audit.

egfr <- 142 * pmin(creatinine / ifelse(female == 1, 0.7, 0.9), 1)^ifelse(female == 1, -0.241, -0.302) * pmax(creatinine / ifelse(female == 1, 0.7, 0.9), 1)^(-1.2) * 0.9938^age * ifelse(female == 1, 1.012, 1)
sbp <- coalesce((BPXOSY1 + BPXOSY2 + BPXOSY3) / 3, (BPXSY1 + BPXSY2 + BPXSY3) / 3)
dbp <- coalesce((BPXODI1 + BPXODI2 + BPXODI3) / 3, (BPXDI1 + BPXDI2 + BPXDI3) / 3)

race_eth <- coalesce(cases(RIDRETH3 == 3, "Non-Hispanic White", RIDRETH3 == 4, "Non-Hispanic Black", RIDRETH3 %in% c(1, 2), "Hispanic", RIDRETH3 == 6, "Non-Hispanic Asian", RIDRETH3 == 7, "Other or multiracial"), cases(RIDRETH1 == 3, "Non-Hispanic White", RIDRETH1 == 4, "Non-Hispanic Black", RIDRETH1 %in% c(1, 2), "Hispanic", RIDRETH1 == 5, "Other or multiracial"))
educ <- cases(DMDEDUC2 %in% c(1, 2), "Less than high school", DMDEDUC2 == 3, "High school or GED", DMDEDUC2 == 4, "Some college", DMDEDUC2 == 5, "College graduate or above")
des <- svydesign(ids = ~SDMVPSU, strata = ~SDMVSTRA, weights = ~WT, nest = TRUE, data = <positive-weight records>)
svyciprop(~I(ckd_kdigo == 1), subset(des, analytic), method = 'beta')  # by sex, agecat, race_eth
svyglm(ckd_kdigo ~ htn_accaha2017 + age + sex + race_eth, design = <demographic>, family = quasipoisson)
svyglm(ckd_kdigo ~ htn_accaha2017 + age + sex + race_eth + pir_cat + diabetes + educ + smoking + bmi, design = <full>, family = quasipoisson)
